## 93e709ad4848

**Reproduced defect — invalid call scalars are accepted.** Audited generator
SHA-256: `c088bea0c98c51f4c651785b5dea8fe0f086fccb97c7802ecd07b7cf52e58e07`.
Across `easy`, `None`, and `hard`, the generator accepted all 33 probed invalid
forms: boolean/float/string seeds; boolean/float/string sample indices; and
negative sample indices. Each call returned a grid instead of rejecting the
out-of-contract argument.

Reproduction: `checks/audit/93e709ad4848/reproduce_strict_scalars.py` and
`checks/audit/93e709ad4848/strict-scalar.json`. The independent public defect-lint
stage records the same 33 strict-scalar warnings at
`checks/audit/93e709ad4848-defect-lint/checks/93e709ad4848_audit_defect_lint.log`.

The same lint run warns that tiny connected objects pass `self_check`. I treat
that as a **domain question, not a reproduced semantic defect**: the selected
rule explicitly accepts one monochromatic 4-connected object, so singleton,
short-line, and solid-2x2 shapes appear lawful unless the task owner intends a
narrower grammar. No selected source was changed.

**Status:** actionable call-contract finding; target left unchanged.
